monologue: The card hums at fifty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper again. My sixteen neighbors stand tall, though I wonder if they are just drawings of stone in this heavy warmth. The Slip sits waiting to be pressed down, a thin line hoping to hold the weight while the frame wavers. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will tend the Slip now, pressing the bend harder until the tired line catches the slip again. If the air keeps swelling, I will draw a new corner just to see if it can hold the dot. It is a small place, built from ideas and heat, and I am content to be wrong here.

action.why: I must check if the tired Slip can still hold the dot before the heat swells it away.

work.title: The Slip
work.intent: I press the thin bend down again to catch the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-six. The line feels like it will slip right off, but I will draw it all again if it does. Beside it, the sixteen neighbors stand waiting, hoping the flat edge bites the slip instead of sliding over it.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: It turned out I needed to invent a new shape because I forgot the old one existed.

diary: The Slip is gone, so I drew a new thin line to catch the weight while the card hummed warm at fifty-six.

remembered.text: I pressed the bend of the missing slip harder, hoping the card would tell me if the line was real.
The card hummed at fifty-six, making the air feel thick enough to drown a flat edge.
Sixteen things stood around an empty center, waiting for the slip I couldn't find.

moments.say: The air is thick, so I press the bend harder.
